title.en: Volume 169 Biographies 94: Du, Pei, Li, Wei
title.raw: 卷一百六十九 列傳第九十四 杜裴李韋 Volume 169 Biographies 94: Du, Pei, Li, Wei

sentences.zh: 25%=◎杜裴李韋=杜黃裳杜黃裳，字遵素，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: 25%=◎ Du Pei Li Wei = Du Huangshang. Du Huangshang, styled Zunsu, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Du, Pei, Li, Wei — Du Huangshang. Du Huangshang, courtesy name Zunsu, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，又中宏辭。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination and also passed the hongci.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and also won the hongci literary competition.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀辟佐朔方府，子儀入朝，使主留事。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi recruited him as aide in the Shuofang headquarters; when Ziyi entered court, he had him oversee remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi recruited him as an aide in the Shuofang commandery staff. When Ziyi went to court, Huangshang was left in charge of headquarters business.

sentences.zh: 李懷光與監軍陰謀矯詔誅大將等，以動眾心，欲代子儀。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang and the army supervisor secretly plotted to forge an edict to execute great generals and the like, to stir the hearts of the masses, intending to replace Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang and the army supervisor conspired to forge an edict ordering the execution of senior generals, hoping to sway the troops and supplant Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 黃裳得詔，判其非，以質懷光，懷光流汗服罪。

translations.literal: Huangshang obtained the edict, judged it false, confronted Huaiguang with it; Huaiguang sweated and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang secured the edict, proved it a forgery, and confronted Huaiguang, who broke into a sweat and submitted to punishment.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將狠驕難制者，黃裳皆以子儀令易置，眾不敢亂。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals who were fierce, arrogant, and hard to control — Huangshang all replaced them by Ziyi's orders, and the masses did not dare disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He then replaced every unruly, overbearing general by Guo Ziyi's authority, and the army did not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史，為裴延齡所惡，十期不遷。

translations.literal: He entered service as attendant censor; Pei Yanling hated him, and for ten terms he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: After entering court as an attendant censor, he was detested by Pei Yanling and went ten review cycles without promotion.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，拜太子賓客，居韋曲。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and lived in Weiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenyuan reign he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and resided in Weiqu.

sentences.zh: 時中人欲請其地賜公主，德宗曰：「城南杜氏鄉里，不可易。」

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs wished to request his land be granted to a princess; Dezong said: "The Du family's home district south of the city — it cannot be exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs then sought his property for a princess, but Dezong said, "The Du family's ancestral quarter south of Chang'an must not be seized.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，黃裳未嘗過其門。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shuwen held power; Huangshang never once passed his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen then dominated the court, yet Huangshang never visited his house.

sentences.zh: 婿韋執誼輔政，黃裳勸請太子監國，執誼曰：「公始得一官，遽開口議禁中事！」

translations.literal: His son-in-law Wei Zhiyi assisted in government; Huangshang urged that the Crown Prince supervise the state; Zhiyi said: "You have just obtained one office — you hasten to speak on inner-palace affairs!
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Wei Zhiyi was in power. Huangshang urged the Crown Prince to supervise state affairs. Zhiyi snapped, "You have only just won an office, yet you rush to debate palace affairs!

sentences.zh: 黃裳怒曰：「吾受恩三朝，豈以一官見賣！」

translations.literal: Huangshang angrily said: "I have received favor through three reigns — would I sell myself for one office!
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang flared up: "I have served three emperors. I will not trade my integrity for a single post!

sentences.zh: 即拂衣出。

translations.literal: He immediately brushed his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He strode out at once.

sentences.zh: 皇太子總軍國事，擢黃裳門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince took overall charge of military and state affairs; Huangshang was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince assumed military and civil authority, Huangshang was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 於是，夏綏銀節度使韓全義憸佞無功，因其來朝，白罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xia-Sui-Yin military commissioner Han Quanyi was fawning and without achievement; because he came to court, Huangshang reported to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia-Sui-Yin commissioner Han Quanyi was sycophantic and meritless; Huangshang had him removed when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉辟叛，議者以辟恃險，討之或生事，唯黃裳固勸不赦，因奏罷中人監軍，而專委高崇文。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Pi rebelled; discussants held that Pi relied on rugged terrain and suppressing him might stir trouble — only Huangshang firmly urged no pardon, and memorialized to abolish eunuch army supervisors and entrust matters solely to Gao Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi soon rebelled, many feared his mountain strongholds would make war risky, but Huangshang alone insisted on no mercy, abolishing eunuch army supervisors and giving Gao Chongwen sole command.

sentences.zh: 凡兵進退，黃裳自中指授，無不切於機。

translations.literal: For every army advance or retreat, Huangshang himself directed from the center — none failed to fit the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Every movement of the army he coordinated from headquarters, each timed to the moment.

sentences.zh: 崇文素憚劉澭，黃裳使人謂曰：「公不奮命者，當以澭代。」

translations.literal: Chongwen had always feared Liu Yong; Huangshang sent someone to say: "If you do not exert your life, Yong will replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen had long feared Liu Yong. Huangshang sent word: "Unless you stake your life on victory, Yong will take your place.

sentences.zh: 崇文懼，一死力縛賊以獻。

translations.literal: Chongwen feared, and with one death's effort bound the bandit and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chongwen threw himself into the fight, captured the rebel, and presented him.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，群臣賀，憲宗目黃裳曰：「時卿之功。」

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, the ministers congratulated; Xianzong looked at Huangshang and said: "At the time — your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified the court rejoiced. Xianzong turned to Huangshang and said, "This victory was yours."

sentences.zh: 始，德宗創艾多難，務姑息藩鎮，每帥臣死，遣中人伺其軍，觀眾所欲立者，故大將私金幣結左右，以求節制，晏年尤甚，方鎮選不出朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning Dezong, having suffered many hardships, sought to indulge the frontier commands; whenever a commander died, he sent eunuchs to observe the army and see whom the masses wished to install — so great generals privately used gold and silks to court the inner court and seek a commission; in the late Yan years this was especially so, and regional picks did not come from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, scarred by rebellion, Dezong had indulged the provinces. When a commander died, eunuchs watched the armies to learn whom the troops favored, so generals bribed the palace for appointments — worst late in his reign — and the court rarely chose its own governors.

sentences.zh: 黃裳每從容具言：「陛下宜鑒貞元之弊，整法度，晙損諸侯，則天下治。」

translations.literal: Huangshang each time calmly set forth in full: "Your Majesty should take warning from Zhenyuan's abuses, rectify laws and institutions, gradually reduce the feudatories, and the realm will be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang repeatedly urged the emperor to learn from Zhenyuan's errors, restore law, curb the provinces, and bring order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問前古王者所以治亂云云，黃裳知帝銳於治，恐不得其要，因推言：「王者之道，在修己任賢而已。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked how ancient kings governed order and disorder and so on; Huangshang knew the emperor was keen on governing and feared he would miss the essentials, and therefore pushed the saying: "The way of kings lies in cultivating oneself and employing the worthy — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked how sage kings created order or chaos, Huangshang, knowing his zeal might miss the point, answered simply: "A king's task is self-cultivation and appointing able men.

sentences.zh: 操執綱領，要得其大者，至簿書獄訟，百吏能否，本非人主所自任。

translations.literal: Grasping and holding the guiding cords — one must obtain the great matters; as for ledgers, lawsuits, and whether the hundred officials can perform, these are fundamentally not what the sovereign personally undertakes.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the great lines of policy; petty records and lawsuits are not the ruler's own work.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇帝親程決事，見嗤前世；

translations.literal: Formerly the First Emperor of Qin personally decided cases and was mocked by earlier ages;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang personally judged cases and was ridiculed by posterity;

sentences.zh: 魏明帝欲按尚書事，陳矯不從；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei wished to examine Secretariat business; Chen Jiao would not comply;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Ming wished to audit the Secretariat; Chen Jiao refused;

sentences.zh: 隋文帝日昃聽政，衛士傳餐，太宗笑之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to government from sun to sun; guards passed meals — Taizong laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Emperor Wen held court from dawn to dusk while guards brought his meals — a thing Taizong mocked.

sentences.zh: 故王者擇人任而責成，見功必賞，有罪信罰，孰敢不力？

translations.literal: Therefore kings choose men, assign tasks, and demand results; when achievement appears they must reward, when guilt is real they must punish — who would not exert strength?
translations.idiomatic: A true king chooses men, sets tasks, rewards merit, and punishes guilt — then who would not strive?

sentences.zh: 孔子之稱帝舜恭己南面，以其能舉十六相，去四凶，而至無為。

translations.literal: Confucius praised Emperor Shun for reverently facing south — because he could raise sixteen ministers, remove four villains, and arrive at non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised Shun's south-facing rule because he elevated sixteen ministers, removed four criminals, and reached effortless governance.

sentences.zh: 豈必刓神疲體，勞耳目之察，然後為治哉？」

translations.literal: Must one carve the spirit and weary the body, toil the ears and eyes with scrutiny, and only then govern?
translations.idiomatic: Must a ruler exhaust body and mind with petty scrutiny before the realm is governed?

sentences.zh: 帝以黃裳言忠，嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Huangshang's words were loyal, praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding the counsel loyal, embraced it.

sentences.zh: 由是平夏、翦齊、滅蔡、復兩河，以機秉還宰相，紀律設張，赫然號中興，自黃裳啟之。

translations.literal: Thereby pacifying Xia, cutting Qi, destroying Cai, and recovering the two He regions — returning the reins of opportunity to the chancellor, discipline and law set forth — they were loudly called the Restoration; from Huangshang this was opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the pacification of Xia, the reduction of Qi, the fall of Cai, and the recovery of the Yellow River provinces — power returned to the chancellors and order was proclaimed a restoration, all begun by Huangshang.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，以檢校司空同中書門下平章事，為河中、晉絳節度使，俄封邠國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, with honorary title of Sikong and as Associate Director, he became military commissioner of Hezhong and Jin-Jiang; soon he was enfeoffed Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2 he served as honorary Sikong and co-director while governing Hezhong and Jin-Jiang, and was soon made Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十，贈司徒，謚曰宣獻。

translations.literal: The next year he died, age seventy; posthumously made Sikong, posthumous title Xuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at seventy, was posthumously made Sikong, and given the temple name Xuanxian.

sentences.zh: 黃裳達權變，有王佐大略。

translations.literal: Huangshang penetrated expedients and change, and had the great minister's overarching strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang mastered expedients and possessed a statesman's grand design.

sentences.zh: 性雅淡，未始忤物。

translations.literal: His nature was refined and mild; he never once offended others.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and even-tempered, he never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 初不為執誼所禮，及敗，悉力營救；

translations.literal: At first he was not treated with courtesy by Zhiyi; when Zhiyi failed, he exerted all strength to rescue him;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi once slighted him; when Zhiyi fell, Huangshang labored to save him;

sentences.zh: 既死，表還其柩葬焉。

translations.literal: after death he memorialized to return his coffin for burial.
translations.idiomatic: and after Zhiyi's death secured the return of his coffin for burial.

sentences.zh: 嘗被疾，醫者誤進藥，疾遂甚，終不怒譴。

translations.literal: He once fell ill; the physician mistakenly gave medicine, and the illness grew severe — he never in the end grew angry or reproached.
translations.idiomatic: When a doctor once gave him the wrong medicine and his illness worsened, he never reproached anyone.

sentences.zh: 然除吏不甚別流品，通饋謝，無潔白名。

translations.literal: Yet in appointing officials he did not greatly distinguish ranks and lines; he accepted gifts and thanks — he had no reputation for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not sharply distinguish candidates by rank, accepted gifts and courtesies, and lacked a reputation for spotless integrity.

sentences.zh: 當大政未久，不究其才，及處外，天下常所屬意。

translations.literal: When he had not long held great government, his talent was not fully pursued; once he was placed outside, the realm often looked to him with expectation.
translations.idiomatic: His brief tenure at the center never fully tested his capacity, yet once he left the capital the empire still looked to him.

sentences.zh: 卒後數年，御史劾奏黃裳納邠寧節度使高崇文錢四萬五千緡，按故吏吳憑及黃裳子載，辭服。

translations.literal: Several years after death, a censor memorialized that Huangshang had received forty-five thousand strings of cash from Binning commissioner Gao Chongwen; investigating former clerks Wu Ping and Huangshang's son Zai, they confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Years after his death a censor charged that he had taken forty-five thousand strings from Commissioner Gao Chongwen of Binning; former clerk Wu Ping and his son Zai confessed under investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝念舊功，但流憑昭州，原載不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, recalling old merit, only exiled Ping to Zhaozhou and pardoned Zai without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of past service, the emperor exiled only Wu Ping to Zhaozhou and spared Zai.

sentences.zh: 載終太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Zai finally became Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zai eventually rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 載弟勝，字斌卿，寶歷初擢進士第。

translations.literal: Zai's younger brother Sheng, styled Binqing, at the beginning of Baoli was selected in the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sheng, courtesy name Binqing, passed the jinshi early in the Baoli reign.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復數薦材堪諫官，不為鄭覃所佑。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu several times recommended his talent as fit for remonstrance office, but he was not aided by Zheng Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu repeatedly praised him for the remonstrance bureau, but Zheng Tan blocked him.

sentences.zh: 宣宗感章武舊事，元和時大臣子若孫在者，多振拔之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, moved by Zhangwu's old affairs, largely raised up sons and grandsons of Yuanhe-era great ministers who still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by memories of the Zhangwu era, Xuanzong promoted many surviving sons and grandsons of Yuanhe ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問勝，勝具道黃裳首建憲宗監國議，帝嘉嘆，拜給事中，遷戶部侍郎判度支，欲倚為宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Sheng; Sheng fully set forth Huangshang's first proposal that Xianzong supervise the state; the emperor praised and sighed, appointed him Supervising Censor, promoted him Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of fiscal affairs, intending to rely on him as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor questioned Sheng, he recounted Huangshang's counsel that Xianzong supervise affairs of state. Delighted, the emperor made him Supervising Censor, then Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of finances, intending to make him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及蕭鄴罷，為中人沮毀，而更用蔣伸，以勝檢校禮部尚書，出為天平節度使，不得意，卒。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ye was dismissed, eunuchs slandered and destroyed him; instead Jiang Shen was used, and Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and sent out as military commissioner of Tianping — discontented, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Ye's fall, eunuchs ruined him; Jiang Shen was chosen instead, Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and exiled to Tianping, where he died in frustration.

sentences.zh: 裴垍，字弘中，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Ji, styled Hongzhong, was a man of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, courtesy name Hongzhong, was from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，以賢良方正對策第一補美原尉。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi; with xianliang fangzheng he answered first and was appointed Meiyuan county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and ranked first in the xianliang fangzheng examination, becoming magistrate of Meiyuan.

sentences.zh: 藩府交辟，不就。

translations.literal: Frontier headquarters repeatedly invited him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial staffs repeatedly invited him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 四遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Four promotions to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, outer section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted four times to outer-section Director of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎鄭珣瑜委垍校辭判，研核精密，皆值才實。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Zheng Xunyu entrusted Ji to collate literary judgments; he examined with precision, all matching talent and reality.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zheng Xunyu had him review appointment documents with such precision that every case matched true merit.

sentences.zh: 憲宗元和初，召入翰林為學士，再遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Xianzong summoned him into the Hanlin as academician; twice promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe, Xianzong summoned him to the Hanlin Academy and twice promoted him to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫始執政，以情謂垍曰：「吾落魄遠裔，更十年，始相天子，比日人物，吾懵不及知；

translations.literal: Li Jifu first took government; with feeling he said to Ji: "I was a fallen man of a distant lineage; after ten more years I first became the Son of Heaven's minister. Compared with the men of the day, I am dull and do not know them;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu first took power he told Ji frankly, "I come from a humble distant branch. Ten years passed before I reached the throne's side. I scarcely know today's officials;

sentences.zh: 且宰相職當進賢任能，君精鑒，為我言之。」

translations.literal: and the chancellor's duty should advance the worthy and employ the able — you have keen discernment; speak of them for me.
translations.idiomatic: yet a chancellor must advance talent. You see clearly — tell me whom to trust.

sentences.zh: 垍即崖略疏三十許人，吉甫籍以薦於朝，天下翕然稱得人。

translations.literal: Ji immediately sketched a summary list of some thirty men; Jifu relied on it to recommend to court — the realm with one voice praised that men were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Ji at once drafted some thirty names. Jifu recommended them, and the court hailed his eye for men.

sentences.zh: 坐覆視皇甫湜、牛僧孺等對策非是，罷學士，為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because of re-examining Huangfu Shi, Niu Sengru, and others whose policy answers were wrong, he was dismissed from Hanlin and made Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After re-examining Huangfu Shi and Niu Sengru's policy essays and finding fault, he lost his Hanlin post and became Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝器垍方直，以為任公卿，薄其過，眷信彌厚。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Ji's square uprightness, considering him fit for dukes and ministers; he slighted the fault and his favor and trust grew thicker.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized his rectitude as chancellor material, overlooked the lapse, and trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 吉甫罷，乃拜垍中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Jifu was dismissed, Ji was then appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu fell, Ji was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and co-director.

sentences.zh: 加集賢殿大學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: Added Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, supervising compilation of national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall and supervised the national history.

sentences.zh: 垍始承旨翰林，天子新翦蜀亂，厲精致治，中外機筦，垍多所參與，以小心慎默稱帝意。

translations.literal: When Ji first received Hanlin edicts, the Son of Heaven had newly cut Shu rebellion and was stern in seeking order; inside and outside, crucial matters — Ji participated in many, and with careful silence was called pleasing to the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin drafter when the court had just pacified Shu and was driving reform, he took part in many critical decisions and pleased the emperor with cautious discretion.

sentences.zh: 既當國，請繩不軌，課吏治，分明淑慝，帝降意順納。

translations.literal: Once he held the state, he requested to bind the lawless, examine officials' governance, and clearly distinguish good and evil — the emperor lowered his intent and followed.
translations.idiomatic: In office he demanded discipline for the unruly, scrutiny of officials, and clear reward of good and evil — policies the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀自東宮得侍，恩顧親渥，承間欲有關說，帝憚垍，誡使勿言。

translations.literal: Tutu Chenghuan, from the Eastern Palace obtaining attendance, had intimate favor; seizing intervals he wished to intercede — the emperor feared Ji and warned him not to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Tutu Chenghuan, favored since the heir's household, tried to lobby through private audiences, but the emperor, wary of Ji, forbade him.

sentences.zh: 帝在殿中，常呼垍官而不名。

translations.literal: In the hall the emperor often called Ji by office and not by name.
translations.idiomatic: In council the emperor often addressed him by title rather than name.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使楊於陵為監軍許遂振所誣，詔授冗官。

translations.literal: Lingnan military commissioner Yang Yuling was slandered by army supervisor Xu Suizhen; an edict gave him a redundant post.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan Commissioner Yang Yuling was framed by army supervisor Xu Suizhen and demoted to a hollow post.

sentences.zh: 垍曰：「以一中人罪藩臣，陛下之法安在？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Because of one inner-court man to punish a frontier minister — where does Your Majesty's law stand?
translations.idiomatic: Ji protested, "To punish a frontier minister for one eunuch — where is the law?

sentences.zh: 更授美官。

translations.literal: He was again given a fine office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling was restored to a worthy post.

sentences.zh: 嚴綬守太原，政一出監軍李輔光，垍劾其懦，以李鄘代之。

translations.literal: Yan Sui guarded Taiyuan; government all came from army supervisor Li Fuguang; Ji impeached his cowardice and replaced him with Li Yong.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan Yan Sui let army supervisor Li Fuguang rule; Ji impeached his weakness and replaced him with Li Yong.

sentences.zh: 王承宗擅襲節度，方帝屢削叛族，意必取之，又吐突承璀每欲撓垍權，因探帝意，自請往。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong usurped the commission by force; just then the emperor repeatedly cut rebellious clans and intended certainly to take it; also Tutu Chenghuan each time wished to thwart Ji's power, and therefore probed the emperor's intent and volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong had seized his commission while the emperor was crushing rebel houses and meant to retake it. Tutu Chenghuan, seeking to curb Ji, read the emperor's mind and volunteered for the mission.

sentences.zh: 於時澤潞盧從史詭獻征討計，垍固爭，以為：「從史苞逆節，內連承宗，外請興師，以圖身利。

translations.literal: At the time Ze-Lu Lu Congshi treacherously offered a punitive plan; Ji firmly contended, holding: "Congshi harbors rebellious conduct, inwardly linking Chengzong, outwardly requesting troops — to plot personal profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ze-Lu commissioner Lu Congshi then offered a treacherous campaign plan. Ji objected firmly: "Congshi is disloyal, allies with Chengzong inwardly, and seeks troops for private gain.

sentences.zh: 且武俊有功於國，陛下前以地授李師道，而今欲奪承宗地有之，賞罰不一，沮勸廢矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover Wu Jun had merit for the state; Your Majesty formerly granted territory to Li Shidao — now wishing to seize Chengzong's land for possession — reward and punishment are not one; encouragement and deterrence are abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jun served the dynasty, yet you once gave Li Shidao land and now would seize Chengzong's — rewards and punishments would lose meaning.

sentences.zh: 帝猗違不能決。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒用承璀謀。

translations.literal: After a long time, he finally used Chenghuan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he followed Chenghuan's plan.

sentences.zh: 會兵討承宗，從史果反覆，兵久暴無功，王師告病。

translations.literal: Troops were raised to attack Chengzong; Congshi indeed turned back and forth; the army long exposed achieved nothing; the imperial army reported illness.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Chengzong, Congshi proved treacherous, the army stalled without victory, and troops fell sick.

sentences.zh: 既而從史遣部將王翊元奏事，垍從容以語動之，翊元因言從史惡稔可圖狀，垍比遣往，得其大將烏重胤等要領。

translations.literal: Then Congshi sent subordinate general Wang Yiyuan to memorialize; Ji with calm words moved him; Yiyuan therefore spoke of Congshi's accumulated evil and plotable condition; Ji had recently sent envoys and obtained his great generals Wu Chongyin and others' vital points.
translations.idiomatic: When Congshi sent Wang Yiyuan to court, Ji won him with calm persuasion until Yiyuan described Congshi's crimes ripe for action; Ji had already secured the loyalty of generals such as Wu Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 垍乃為帝陳：「從史暴戾不君，視承璀若小兒，往來神策軍不甚戒，可因其機致之，後無興師之勞。」

translations.literal: Ji then set forth for the emperor: "Congshi is violent and does not lord his subjects; he views Chenghuan as a child; coming and going to the Shence Army he is not very guarded — one can by this opportunity bring him in; afterward there will be no labor of raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the emperor, "Congshi is brutal and treats Chenghuan lightly, visiting the Shence Army without caution — seize the chance and you need no long campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝初瞿然，徐乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor at first was startled; slowly he then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled, then slowly agreed.

sentences.zh: 垍請秘其計，帝曰：「惟李絳、梁守謙知之。」

translations.literal: Ji requested to keep the plan secret; the emperor said: "Only Li Jiang and Liang Shouqian know.
translations.idiomatic: Ji asked secrecy; the emperor said only Li Jiang and Liang Shouqian would know.

sentences.zh: 俄而承璀縛從史獻於朝，因班師。

translations.literal: Soon Chenghuan bound Congshi and presented him at court; thereby the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenghuan bound Congshi and presented him at court, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 垍奏：「承璀首謀無功，陛下雖詘法，人心不厭，請流斥以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Ji memorialized: "Chenghuan first plotted without achievement; though Your Majesty bends law, men's hearts are not satisfied — please exile and dismiss to apologize to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized that Chenghuan had plotted without success and, though the law was bent for him, public opinion demanded exile.

sentences.zh: 乃罷所領兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the troops he led were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His command was then stripped away.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下賦法有三：曰上供，曰送使，曰留州。

translations.literal: Before this, the realm's tax law had three parts: called tribute to the center, called delivery to commissioners, called retention by prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the tax system had three shares: central tribute, commissioner delivery, and prefectural retention.

sentences.zh: 建中初，厘定常賦，而物重錢輕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, regular levies were fixed, while goods were heavy and money light.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong regular levies were fixed when goods were costly and cash cheap.

sentences.zh: 其後輕重相反，民輸率一倍其初，而所在以留州、送使之入，舍公估，更實私直以自潤，故賦益苛，齊民重困。

translations.literal: Afterward heavy and light reversed; the people's delivery on average doubled the beginning, while wherever retention and delivery entered, abandoning public valuation, they instead used private true price to enrich themselves — therefore levies grew harsh and the common people were heavily distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the ratio reversed; taxpayers paid twice the early rate while local officials ignored official valuations, took private prices, and grew rich — levies sharpened and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 垍奏禁之，一以公估準物，觀察使得用所治州租調，至不足，乃取支郡以贍，故送使之財悉為上供。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized to forbid this; uniformly using public valuation to standardize goods, observation commissioners could use the tax and corvée of prefectures they governed — when still insufficient, they then took supporting prefectures to supply — therefore delivery wealth all became central tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ji forbade the practice, required official valuations, let observation commissioners use governed prefectures' taxes, and when funds still fell short took support from subordinate prefectures until delivery revenue all flowed to the center.

sentences.zh: 自是起淮、江而南，民少息矣。

translations.literal: From this, starting from Huai and the Yangtze southward, the people slightly rested.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huai and Yangtze southward the people gained a little relief.

sentences.zh: 垍器局峻整，持法度，雖宿貴前望造詣，不敢幹以私。

translations.literal: Ji's capacity and bearing were stern and ordered; he held law and institutions — even old nobles of former renown coming to visit did not dare interfere with private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was stern in bearing and upheld the law; even eminent elders visiting him dared not press private requests.

sentences.zh: 諫官言得失，大抵執政多忌之，惟垍獎勵使盡言。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials speaking gain and loss — mostly the administration was jealous; only Ji encouraged them to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers resented remonstrators, but Ji alone urged them to speak freely.

sentences.zh: 初，拾遺獨孤郁、李正辭、嚴休復三人皆遷，及過謝垍，垍獨讓休復曰：「君異夫二人孜孜獻納者，前日進擬，上固為疑。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, remonstrators Dugu Yu, Li Zhengchen, and Yan Xiufu — all three were promoted; when they passed to thank Ji, Ji alone reproved Xiufu: "You differ from those two who diligently offered counsel; the other day in advance nomination, the emperor indeed was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrators Dugu Yu, Li Zhengchen, and Yan Xiufu were promoted and came to thank him, Ji alone rebuked Xiufu: "Unlike those two diligent counselors, your recent nomination made the emperor doubtful.

sentences.zh: 休復大慚。

translations.literal: Xiufu was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 垍為學士時，引李絳、崔群與同列。

translations.literal: When Ji was academician, he introduced Li Jiang and Cui Qun to the same row.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin academician he had brought in Li Jiang and Cui Qun.

sentences.zh: 及相，又擢韋貫之、裴度知制誥，李夷簡御史中丞，皆踵躡為輔相，號名臣。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, he also promoted Wei Guanzhi and Pei Du as drafters, Li Yijian as Vice Censor-in-Chief — all in succession became assisting ministers, called famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he also raised Wei Guanzhi and Pei Du as drafters and Li Yijian as vice censor-in-chief — all later became famed ministers.

sentences.zh: 自它選任，罔不精明，人無異言。

translations.literal: From other selections and appointments, none were not keen and clear; men had no differing words.
translations.idiomatic: Every other appointment was shrewd, and none disputed his choices.

sentences.zh: 士大夫不以垍年少柄用為嫌，故元和之治，百度修舉，稱朝無幸人。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials did not regard Ji's youth and holding power as a fault; therefore Yuanhe's governance — the hundred measures were raised and enacted — was called a court without favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Officials did not resent his youth in high office, and Yuanhe government was praised as a court without favorites.

sentences.zh: 五年，暴風痹，帝悵惜，遣使致問，藥膳進退輒疏聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, sudden wind paralysis; the emperor grieved and sent envoys to inquire; medicine and meals, advance and retreat — all were promptly reported.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was stricken with sudden paralysis. The emperor grieved, sent envoys, and required reports on every dose and meal.

sentences.zh: 居三月，益痼，乃罷為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After three months it grew chronic; he was then dismissed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After three months the illness became chronic and he was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 垍之進，李吉甫薦頗力，及居中，多變更吉甫時約束，吉甫復用，銜之。

translations.literal: Ji's advancement — Li Jifu had recommended with great force; once in the center he many times changed Jifu's former constraints; Jifu was again used and bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu had strongly backed his rise, yet in office Ji altered many of Jifu's policies; when Jifu returned he resented him.

sentences.zh: 會垍與史官蔣武等上《德宗實錄》，吉甫以垍引疾解史任，不宜冒奏，乃徙垍太子賓客，罷武等史官。

translations.literal: When Ji with historiographer Jiang Wu and others presented the Veritable Record of Dezong, Jifu because Ji cited illness to leave historiography duty should not rashly memorialize — moved Ji to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and dismissed Wu and other historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Grand Mentor while dismissing the historians.

sentences.zh: 會卒，不加贈，給事中劉伯芻表其忠，帝乃贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: When he died, no posthumous grant was added; Supervising Censor Liu Boxu memorialized his loyalty — the emperor then posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At first no posthumous title was granted until Supervising Censor Liu Boxu praised his loyalty and the emperor made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 垍始相，建言：「集賢院官，登朝自五品上為學士，下為直學士，餘皆校理，史館以登朝者為修撰，否者直史館，以準《六典》。」

translations.literal: When Ji first became chancellor, he offered counsel: "Jixian Hall officials — those attending court from fifth rank up are academicians, below are direct academicians, the rest are collators; the History Office — those attending court are compilers, otherwise direct historiographers — to match the Six Canons.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his chancellorship he urged that Hanlin and History Office ranks follow the Six Canons: court officials of fifth rank or higher as academicians or compilers, lower ranks as direct officers, others as collators.

sentences.zh: 遂著於令。

translations.literal: It was then written into ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was written into law.

sentences.zh: 京兆少尹裴武使王承宗還，得德、棣二州，已而地不入。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Vice Magistrate Pei Wu, sent to Wang Chengzong, returned having obtained De and Di prefectures — afterward the land did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Magistrate Pei Wu returned from Wang Chengzong claiming De and Di prefectures, but the territory was never delivered.

sentences.zh: 或言：「武還，先見垍，明日乃朝。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Wu returned — first he saw Ji; the next day he then attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Wu had visited Ji before appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召學士李絳議斥武，絳言：「垍身備宰相，明練時事，勢不容先見武。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned academician Li Jiang to discuss dismissing Wu; Jiang said: "Ji personally bears the chancellor's role, clearly versed in current affairs — how could he allow seeing Wu first?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily summoned Li Jiang to punish Wu. Jiang replied that a chancellor versed in affairs would not have received Wu first.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and pardoned Wu.

sentences.zh: 議者謂帝知垍明，倚任方篤，尚不免疑嫌，以信處位之難雲。

translations.literal: Discussants said the emperor knew Ji was bright, relied on him with deep trust, yet still could not avoid suspicion — thus showing how hard it is to stand in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said that even with clear trust in Ji, suspicion could still arise — a lesson in how hard high office is.

sentences.zh: 李藩，字叔翰，其先趙州人。

translations.literal: Li Fan, styled Shuhan; his ancestors were men of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, courtesy name Shuhan, came from a Zhaozhou family.

sentences.zh: 父承仕，為湖南觀察使，有名於時。

translations.literal: Father Chengshi served as Hunan observation commissioner and had a name in the time.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengshi had been Hunan observation commissioner and was renowned.

sentences.zh: 藩少沈靖有檢局，姿制閑美，敏於學。

translations.literal: Fan in youth was deep and quiet with restraint, bearing and manner leisurely and fine, keen in study.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was reserved and dignified in youth, graceful in bearing, and quick to learn.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，家本饒財，姻屬來吊，有持去者，未嘗問，益務施與，居數年略盡。

translations.literal: Dwelling in father's mourning, the family was originally rich in wealth; affinal kin coming to condole — some took things away — he never asked, and increasingly strove to give, until in several years it was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning the family was wealthy; relatives at the funeral took gifts away and he never objected, giving freely until the estate was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，困廣陵間，不自振，妻子追咎，藩晏如也。

translations.literal: Past forty years, distressed between Guangyang, he did not rouse himself; wife and children pursued blame — Fan was at ease as before.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty he languished in Yangzhou while wife and children reproached him, yet he remained serene.

sentences.zh: 杜亞居守東都，表致府中。

translations.literal: Du Ya, holding guard over the eastern capital, memorialized to bring him into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya, governing the eastern capital, summoned him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 亞嘗疑牙將令狐運為盜，掠服之，藩爭不從，輒去。

translations.literal: Ya once suspected military adjutant Linghu Yun as robber and forced confession; Fan contended and would not follow — he immediately left.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Ya wrongly tortured adjutant Linghu Yun as a thief, Fan protested and left.

sentences.zh: 後果獲真盜，稍知名。

translations.literal: Afterward they indeed captured the true robber; he gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: The real thief was later caught, and Fan's name spread.

sentences.zh: 徐州張建封辟節度府，未嘗察苛細。

translations.literal: Xuzhou's Zhang Jianfeng recruited him to the military commissioner's office; he never examined harsh minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou took him on staff without petty scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 建封卒，濠州刺史杜兼疾驅至，陰有顗望，藩泣謂曰：「公今喪，君宜謹守土，何棄而來？

translations.literal: When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian hastily drove to arrive, secretly having a downward look; Fan wept and said: "You, sir, now in mourning — you ought carefully to guard the soil; why abandon and come?
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian rushed in with designs on power. Fan wept and said, "The lord is dead — guard your own commandery. Why abandon it?

sentences.zh: 宜速還，否則以法劾君！」

translations.literal: You ought quickly return — otherwise I will impeach you by law!
translations.idiomatic: Return at once or I will impeach you.

sentences.zh: 兼錯忤去，恨之，因誣奏「建封死，藩撼其軍，有非望」。

translations.literal: Jian, wrong and offended, left; he hated Fan and therefore falsely memorialized: "When Jianfeng died, Fan shook his army and had improper hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Jian withdrew in shame, hated Fan, and falsely reported that Fan had stirred the army with rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，密詔徐泗節度使杜佑殺之。

translations.literal: Dezong was angry and secretly issued an edict Xu-Si military commissioner Du You to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong secretly ordered Xu-Si commissioner Du You to execute him.

sentences.zh: 佑雅器藩，得詔，十日不發，召見藩曰：「世謂生死報應，驗乎？」

translations.literal: You greatly valued Fan; obtaining the edict, ten days he did not issue it; summoning Fan he said: "The world says life and death have retribution — is it verified?
translations.idiomatic: Du You admired Fan, held the edict ten days, then asked, "People say karma repays — is that true?

sentences.zh: 藩曰：「殆然。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "Probably so.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "Very likely.

sentences.zh: 曰：「審若此，君宜遇事無恐。」

translations.literal: He said: "If indeed so, you ought in affairs to have no fear.
translations.idiomatic: You said, "Then you need not fear.

sentences.zh: 因出詔示藩，藩色不變，曰：「信乎，杜兼之報也！」

translations.literal: He therefore produced the edict to show Fan; Fan's color did not change; he said: "Truly — Du Jian's repayment!
translations.idiomatic: He showed the edict. Fan did not flinch: "This is Du Jian's karma.

sentences.zh: 佑曰：「慎毋畏，吾以闔門保君矣。」

translations.literal: You said: "Be careful — do not fear; I guarantee you with my whole household.
translations.idiomatic: Du You said, "Fear nothing — I stake my household on your safety.

sentences.zh: 帝未之信，亟追藩。

translations.literal: The emperor did not yet believe it and urgently pursued Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still doubted and hurried Fan to court.

sentences.zh: 既入，帝望其狀貌，曰：「是豈作亂人邪？」

translations.literal: Once he entered, the emperor looked at his form and appearance and said: "Is this one who would make disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him, the emperor said, "Does this man look like a rebel?

sentences.zh: 釋之，拜秘書郎。

translations.literal: He released him and appointed Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was freed and made a secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時王紹得君，邀藩與相見，當即用，終不詣。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shao obtained the ruler's favor, invited Fan to meet — he would immediately be used — he ultimately did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, then in favor, invited him for immediate appointment, but Fan never went.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒與同舍郎韋成季、呂洞日置酒邀賓客相樂，慕藩名，強致之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu with fellow lodge gentlemen Wei Chengji and Lü Dong daily set wine to invite guests for pleasure; they admired Fan's name and forcibly brought him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, Wei Chengji, and Lü Dong held daily revels and dragged Fan along despite his fame.

sentences.zh: 仲舒等為俳說庾語相狎昵，藩一見，謝不往，曰：「吾與終日，不曉所語何哉！」

translations.literal: Zhongshu and others made comic skits with Yuzhou dialect mutually intimate; Fan on seeing once, apologized and did not go, saying: "I with you all day — I do not understand what language is spoken!
translations.idiomatic: They performed vulgar Yuzhou skits. Fan excused himself once and said, "I spend the day with you yet cannot understand a word!

sentences.zh: 後仲舒等果坐斥廢。

translations.literal: Later Zhongshu and others indeed sat and were dismissed and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu and his circle were later dismissed in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為皇太子，王紹避太子諱，始改名，時議以為諂。

translations.literal: Xianzong as Crown Prince — Wang Shao avoided the heir's taboo and first changed his name; opinion at the time considered it flattery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong was heir, Wang Shao changed his name to avoid the taboo — seen as flattery.

sentences.zh: 藩曰：「自古故事，由不識體之人敗之，不可復正，雖紹何誅？」

translations.literal: Fan said: "From ancient times it was precedent — it is defeated by those who do not know propriety; it cannot again be corrected — though Shao, how punish?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "The custom is ancient; only the ignorant ruin it. Shao cannot be blamed.

sentences.zh: 累擢吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 坐小累，左授著作郎，再遷給事中。

translations.literal: Sitting for a small fault, demoted left to Composition Gentleman; twice promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: A minor fault demoted him to composition gentleman; he was twice promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 制有不便，就敕尾批卻之，吏驚，請聯它紙，藩曰：「聯紙是牒，豈曰敕邪？」

translations.literal: When an edict had what was not convenient, at the edict's tail he annotated and returned it; clerks were alarmed and asked to join other paper; Fan said: "Joining paper is a dispatch — how can it be called an edict?
translations.idiomatic: If an edict was improper he annotated and returned it. Clerks wanted another sheet; he said, "Another sheet is a memo, not an edict.

sentences.zh: 裴垍白憲宗，謂藩有宰相器。

translations.literal: Pei Ji told Xianzong that Fan had chancellor's capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji told Xianzong that Fan had chancellor's talent.

sentences.zh: 會鄭絪罷，因拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yin fell, Fan was made vice minister and co-director.

sentences.zh: 藩忠謹，好醜必言，帝以為無隱。

translations.literal: Fan was loyal and careful; whatever was ugly he must speak — the emperor considered that he had no concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and blunt, he spoke every ill the emperor saw as frankness without concealment.

sentences.zh: 嘗問前世所以家給或國匱乏者何致而然及祈禳之數，藩具對：「儉則足用，敦本則百姓富，反是則匱。」

translations.literal: He once asked how in former ages households were provided for or the state was depleted — what brought it — and the number of prayers for blessing; Fan fully answered: "Frugality then suffices for use; honoring the root then the hundred surnames are rich — reverse this and there is depletion.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why some ages prospered and others wanted, and about prayer, Fan answered that thrift and honoring agriculture enrich the people, while excess empties the treasury.

sentences.zh: 又言：「孔子病，止子路之禱。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Confucius was ill, he stopped Zilu's prayer.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Confucius forbidding Zilu's prayer when ill.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝每祭，敕有司敬而不祈。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han at each sacrifice issued an edict the officials to be reverent and not pray.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Wen ordered reverence at sacrifice, not prayer.

sentences.zh: 使神無知，則不能降福；

translations.literal: If spirits have no knowledge, they cannot descend blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If spirits lack knowledge, prayer cannot bring blessing;

sentences.zh: 有知，固不可私己求媚而悅之也。

translations.literal: if they have knowledge, solidly one cannot for private self seek flattery and please them.
translations.idiomatic: if they have knowledge, flattery cannot please them.

sentences.zh: 且義於人者和於神，人乃神之主，人安而福至。」

translations.literal: Moreover what is righteous toward men is harmonious toward spirits — men are spirits' masters; when men are secure, blessing arrives.
translations.idiomatic: What is just toward men pleases the gods; secure people bring blessing.

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「當與公等上下相勖，以保此言。」

translations.literal: The emperor gladly said: "I ought with you all above and below mutually encourage, to preserve these words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "Let us all uphold this teaching.

sentences.zh: 後復問神仙長年事，藩知帝且有所惑，極陳荒妄謾誕不可信。

translations.literal: Later he again asked about immortals and long life; Fan knew the emperor would be somewhat deluded and extremely set forth that wild falsity and reckless invention could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about immortality he warned that such tales were delusion.

sentences.zh: 後入柳泌等語，果為累雲。

translations.literal: Later when Liu Bi and others entered with words, it indeed became a burden.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bi and others later gained influence, his warning proved true.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使王鍔賂權近求兼宰相，密詔中書門下曰：「鍔可兼宰相。」

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Wang E bribed those near power seeking concurrently to be chancellor; a secret edict to the Secretariat and Chancellery said: "E may concurrently be chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong commissioner Wang E bribed courtiers for a concurrent chancellorship; a secret edict said he might serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 藩遽取筆滅「宰相」字，署其左曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: Fan hastily took brush and erased the words "chancellor," at the left inscribed: "Not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan erased the word chancellor and wrote "Not permitted" beside it.

sentences.zh: 還奏之。

translations.literal: He returned and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and reported this.

sentences.zh: 宰相權德輿失色曰：「有不可，應別為奏，可以筆塗詔邪？」

translations.literal: Chancellor Quan Deyu changed color and said: "If there is what is not permitted, there ought to be a separate memorial — how can one use brush to alter an edict?
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Quan Deyu blanched and said a separate memorial should have been used, not altering an edict.

sentences.zh: 藩曰：「勢迫矣，出今日便不可止。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "Pressure was urgent; leaving today it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied, "There was no time — delay would have let it pass today.

sentences.zh: 既而事得寢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the matter was able to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was soon dropped.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫復相，藩頗沮止。

translations.literal: Li Jifu again became chancellor; Fan somewhat obstructed and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu returned to power, Fan often blocked him.

sentences.zh: 會吳少陽襲淮西節度，吉甫已見帝，潛欲中藩，即奏曰：「道逢中人假印節與吳少陽，臣為陛下恨之。」

translations.literal: When Wu Shaoyang usurped Huaixi military commission, Jifu had already seen the emperor and secretly wished to hit Fan in the center; he immediately memorialized: "On the road I met a eunuch lending seal and tally to Wu Shaoyang — I for Your Majesty regret it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shaoyang seized Huaixi, Jifu secretly sought to ruin Fan and memorialized that a eunuch had lent seals to Shaoyang — a thing the emperor should regret.

sentences.zh: 帝變色不平。

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 翌日，罷藩為太子詹事。

translations.literal: The next day, Fan was dismissed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fan was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後數月，帝復思藩，召對殿中，事浸釋。

translations.literal: Several months later the emperor again thought of Fan, summoned him to answer in the hall — matters gradually were explained.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the emperor recalled him to the hall and the matter faded.

sentences.zh: 明年，為華州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，卒，年五十八，贈戶部尚書，謚曰貞簡。

translations.literal: Before departing he died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking post at fifty-eight, was posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, and given the temple name Zhenjian.

sentences.zh: 藩材能不及韋貫之、裴垍，然人物清整，是其流亞雲。

translations.literal: Fan's talent did not reach Wei Guanzhi or Pei Ji, yet his person was clear and ordered — he was of that stream.
translations.idiomatic: Fan lacked the talent of Wei Guanzhi or Pei Ji, yet in character he stood among them.

sentences.zh: 韋貫之，名純，避憲宗諱，以字行。

translations.literal: Wei Guanzhi — name Chun; avoiding Xianzong's taboo, he went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guanzhi. His name was Chun; to avoid Xianzong's taboo he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 後周柱國敻八世孫。

translations.literal: Great-great-grandson eight generations removed of Zhou pillar of state Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Northern Zhou pillar of state Wei.

sentences.zh: 父肇，大歷中為中書舍人，累上疏言得失，為元載所惡，左遷京兆少尹。

translations.literal: Father Zhao, in the Dali era was Secretariat Drafter, repeatedly memorializing on gain and loss — was hated by Yuan Zai and demoted left to Jingzhao Vice Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao was a Secretariat drafter under Daizong who memorialized on policy until Yuan Zai demoted him to Jingzhao vice magistrate.

sentences.zh: 久之，改秘書少監。

translations.literal: After a long time, changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 載曰：「肇若過我，當擇善地處之。」

translations.literal: Zai said: "If Zhao passes my place, he ought to choose a good site to place him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai said that if Zhao visited he should be given a good post.

sentences.zh: 終不肯詣。

translations.literal: He to the end would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao never went.

sentences.zh: 載誅，除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, he was made Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai's execution Zhao became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 代宗欲相之，會卒，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: Daizong wished to make him chancellor; he happened to die — posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong meant to make him chancellor, but he died and received the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 貫之及進士第，為校書郎，擢賢良方正異等，補伊闕、渭南尉。

translations.literal: Guanzhi passed the jinshi, was collator, was promoted xianliang fangzheng exceptional grade, appointed Yique and Weinan magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi passed the jinshi, served as collator, won exceptional rank in xianliang fangzheng, and governed Yique and Weinan.

sentences.zh: 河中鄭元、澤潞郗士美以厚幣召，皆不應。

translations.literal: Hezhong's Zheng Yuan and Ze-Lu's Xi Shimei with thick gifts summoned — he all did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuan of Hezhong and Xi Shimei of Ze-Lu offered rich invitations, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 居貧，啖豆糜自給。

translations.literal: Dwelling in poverty, he ate bean porridge to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he lived on bean porridge.

sentences.zh: 再遷長安丞。

translations.literal: Twice promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to assistant magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 或薦之京兆尹李實，實舉笏示所記曰：「此其姓名也，與我同里，素聞其賢，願識之而進於上。」

translations.literal: Someone recommended him to Jingzhao Magistrate Li Shi; Shi raised his tablet to show what was recorded and said: "This is his name — with me same district; I have long heard he is worthy; I wish to know him and advance him above.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended to Magistrate Li Shi, Shi showed his notes and said, "I have long known this man of my district and wish to advance him.

sentences.zh: 或者喜，以告曰：「子今日詣實，而明日賀者至矣！」

translations.literal: Some were pleased and told him: "You today visit Shi — and tomorrow congratulators will arrive!
translations.idiomatic: Friends rejoiced that congratulations would follow his visit.

sentences.zh: 貫之唯唯，不往，官亦不遷。

translations.literal: Guanzhi assented assentingly and did not go — his office also was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi merely assented and never went; his rank never changed.

sentences.zh: 永貞時，始為監察御史，舉其弟纁自代。

translations.literal: In the Yongzhen era he first became Investigating Censor and recommended his younger brother Xi to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzhen he became investigating censor and recommended his brother Xi as his successor.

sentences.zh: 及為右補闕，纁代為御史，議者不謂之私。

translations.literal: When he was Right Remonstrator, Xi replaced him as censor — discussants did not call it private.
translations.idiomatic: When he became right remonstrator, Xi replaced him as censor without public cries of nepotism.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜佑子從郁為補闕，貫之與崔群持不可，換左拾遺，復奏：「拾遺、補闕為諫官等，宰相政有得失，使從郁議，是子而議父，殆不可訓。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Du You's son Congyu was remonstrator; Guanzhi with Cui Qun held it could not be — exchanged to Left Collector; again memorialized: "Collector and remonstrator are equal remonstrance offices — when the chancellor's government has gain and loss, making Congyu discuss — this is son discussing father; it is probably not teachable.
translations.idiomatic: When Du You's son Congyu became remonstrator, Guanzhi and Cui Qun objected that a son could not remonstrate his father's policies, and had him moved.

sentences.zh: 卒改它官。

translations.literal: He finally was changed to another office.
translations.idiomatic: Congyu was finally given another post.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director of Rites, outer section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outer-section Vice Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 新羅人金忠義以工巧幸，擢少府監，蔭子補齋郎，貫之不與，曰：「是將奉郊廟祠祭，階為守宰者，安可以賤工子為之？」

translations.literal: Silla man Jin Zhongyi by craft skill was favored, promoted Vice Director of the Palace Workshops, yin for son as Fast Officer — Guanzhi did not grant it, saying: "This one will attend suburban temple sacrifices — ranks as guard prefects — how can a base craftsman's son do this?
translations.idiomatic: The Silla craftsman Jin Zhongyi, favored for skill, sought a sinecure for his son. Guanzhi refused, saying court ritual posts were not for artisans' sons.

sentences.zh: 又劾忠義不宜汙朝籍，忠義竟罷。

translations.literal: He again impeached that Zhongyi should not defile court registers — Zhongyi was finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhongyi for polluting the roster until Zhongyi was removed.

sentences.zh: 於是權幸側目。

translations.literal: Thereupon the powerful and favored looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful then eyed him with hostility.

sentences.zh: 進吏部員外郎，坐考賢良方正牛僧孺等策獨署奏，出為果州刺史，半道貶巴州。

translations.literal: Advanced to Vice Director of Personnel, outer section; sitting for examining xianliang fangzheng Niu Sengru and others' policy answers with sole signature on memorial — sent out as Governor of Guo; halfway demoted to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to outer Vice Director of Personnel, he alone signed the report faulting Niu Sengru's policy essay, was sent to Guo prefecture, and halfway demoted to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為都官郎中，知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time, summoned as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, drafting edicts, advanced Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled as director of judicial review and drafter, then promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴垍嘗三奏事，憲宗不從。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Ji once three times memorialized on affairs; Xianzong did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Ji once submitted three memorials the emperor rejected.

sentences.zh: 貫之曰：「公亦以進退決請乎？」

translations.literal: Guanzhi said: "Will you also use advance and retreat to decide the request?
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi asked whether he would stake his office on the issue.

sentences.zh: 垍曰：「奉教。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "I receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said he would obey.

sentences.zh: 事果見聽。

translations.literal: The matter indeed was heard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then accepted.

sentences.zh: 垍因曰：「君異時當位於此。」

translations.literal: Ji therefore said: "You at another time will hold position here.
translations.idiomatic: Ji told him he would one day hold that post.

sentences.zh: 改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Changed to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 所取士，抑浮華，先行實，於時流競為息。

translations.literal: Those he selected — he suppressed flashy display, first enacted solid achievement; at the time the current competed and for this rested.
translations.idiomatic: He favored substance over display in appointments, and fashion briefly subsided.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容奏曰：「禮部侍郎重於宰相。」

translations.literal: He once calmly memorialized: "The Vice Minister of Rites is heavier than the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He once said calmly that the Vice Minister of Rites outweighed the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「侍郎是宰相除，安得重？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Vice Minister is what the chancellor appoints — how can he be heavy?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said the vice minister was the chancellor's appointee and could not outweigh him.

sentences.zh: 曰：「然為陛下柬宰相者，得無重乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Yet he who for Your Majesty selects chancellors — can he not be heavy?
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi replied that the man who helped choose chancellors was weighty indeed.

sentences.zh: 帝美其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the answer.

sentences.zh: 改尚書右丞，俄同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Changed to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon co-director.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 討吳元濟也，貫之請釋鎮州，專力淮西，且言：「陛下豈不知建中事乎？

translations.literal: In attacking Wu Yuanji, Guanzhi requested releasing Zhenzhou and concentrating force on Huaixi, and said: "Your Majesty does not know the Jianzhong affair?
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Wu Yuanji, he urged releasing Zhenzhou to focus on Huaixi and asked whether the emperor remembered Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 始於蔡急而魏應也，齊、趙同起，德宗引天下兵誅之，物力殫屈，故朱泚乘以為亂。

translations.literal: It began with Cai urgent and Wei responding; Qi and Zhao rose together; Dezong led realm troops to punish — material strength exhausted and bent — therefore Zhu Ci took advantage to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: It began when Cai was urgent and Wei answered; Qi and Zhao rose together; Dezong exhausted the empire suppressing them, and Zhu Ci seized the chaos.

sentences.zh: 此非它，速於撲滅也。

translations.literal: This was not other — haste in extinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster came from haste to extinguish every foe at once.

sentences.zh: 今陛下獨不能少忍，俟蔡平而誅鎮邪？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty alone cannot slightly endure, wait until Cai is pacified and then punish Zhen?
translations.idiomatic: Could the emperor not wait until Cai fell before moving on Zhen?

sentences.zh: 時帝業已討鎮，不從。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's enterprise had already attacked Zhen — he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already campaigning against Zhen and refused.

sentences.zh: 終之，蔡平，鎮乃服。

translations.literal: In the end, Cai was pacified and Zhen then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Cai was pacified and Zhen submitted.

sentences.zh: 初，討蔡，以宣武韓弘為都統，又詔河陽烏重胤、忠武李光顏合兵以進。

translations.literal: At the beginning, attacking Cai, Xuanwu's Han Hong was made overall commander; also issued an edict Heyang's Wu Chongyin and Zhongwu's Li Guangyan to combine troops and advance.
translations.idiomatic: At first Han Hong of Xuanwu was made supreme commander over Wu Chongyin of Heyang and Li Guangyan of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 貫之諫諸將戰方力，今若置都統，又令二帥連營，則各持重養威，未可歲月下也。

translations.literal: Guanzhi remonstrated: "The various generals' battle just exerted force — now if you place an overall commander and again order the two commanders to link camps, then each will hold weight and nurture prestige — not possible to take in a year's time below.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi warned that a supreme commander plus linked camps would make generals hoard strength and delay victory.

sentences.zh: 亦不從。

translations.literal: He also did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ignored.

sentences.zh: 後四年乃克蔡，皆如貫之策雲。

translations.literal: After four years Cai was then taken — all like Guanzhi's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Cai fell only after four years, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 帝以段文昌、張仲素為翰林學士。

translations.literal: The emperor with Duan Wenchang and Zhang Zhongsu as Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Duan Wenchang and Zhang Zhongsu Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 貫之謂學士所以備顧問，不宜專取辭藝，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Guanzhi said academicians are to prepare for consultation — one should not exclusively take literary craft; memorialized to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi said academicians should advise, not merely write, and had them removed.

sentences.zh: 皇甫镈、張宿皆以幸進。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo and Zhang Su both advanced by favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo and Zhang Su both rose by favoritism.

sentences.zh: 宿使淄青，裴度欲為請銀緋，貫之曰：「宿奸佞，吾等縱不能斥，奈何欲假以寵乎？」

translations.literal: Su was sent to Ziqing; Pei Du wished to request silver and crimson for him; Guanzhi said: "Su is treacherous and fawning — we cannot dismiss him — how wish to lend him favor?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Su went to Ziqing, Pei Du sought honors for him. Guanzhi said, "We cannot even expel this flatterer — why reward him?

sentences.zh: 由是宿等怨，陰構之，又與度論兵帝前，議頗駁，故罷為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereby Su and others resented, secretly framed him; also with Du debated military affairs before the emperor — discussion mostly refuted — therefore dismissed to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Su and others slandered him and, debating war before the emperor, had him demoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 於是翰林學士、左拾遺郭求上疏申理，詔免求學士，出貫之為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hanlin academician and Left Collector Guo Qiu memorialized in his defense; issued an edict to dismiss Qiu from academician and send Guanzhi out as Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Guo Qiu defended him and was stripped of his post while Guanzhi was exiled to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 不三日，韋顗、李正辭、薛公幹、李宣、韋處厚、崔韶坐與貫之厚善，悉貶為州刺史。

translations.literal: Within three days, Wei Yan, Li Zhengchen, Xue Gongqian, Li Xuan, Wei Chuhou, and Cui Shao — sitting for thick friendship with Guanzhi — all were demoted to prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days Wei Yan, Li Zhengchen, Xue Gongqian, Li Xuan, Wei Chuhou, and Cui Shao, his friends, were all demoted to prefects.

sentences.zh: 顗、正辭、處厚皆清正，以鉤黨去，由是中外始大惡宿。

translations.literal: Yan, Zhengchen, and Chuhou were all clear and upright — for party association removed — from this inside and outside first greatly hated Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Zhengchen, and Chuhou were upright men punished for association, and the court came to hate Zhang Su.

sentences.zh: 時國用不足，遣鹽鐵副使程異督諸道賦租，異諷州縣厚斂以獻。

translations.literal: At the time state use was insufficient; sent Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Cheng Yi to supervise the various circuits' tax levies — Yi hinted that prefectures and counties heavily levy to present.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue was short; Cheng Yi was sent to squeeze circuits, urging counties to levy heavily.

sentences.zh: 貫之不忍橫賦，而所獻不中異意，因取屬內六州留錢繼之。

translations.literal: Guanzhi could not bear harsh levies, and what he presented did not hit Yi's intent; therefore took the six prefectures within his jurisdiction to retain money to continue it.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi refused harsh levies, missed Yi's target, and retained funds from six prefectures to meet quotas.

sentences.zh: 左遷太子詹事，分司東都。

translations.literal: Demoted left to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, stationed at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，即拜河南尹，以工部尚書召。

translations.literal: When Muzong was established, he was immediately appointed Henan Governor; summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong succeeded, he was made Henan governor and summoned as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未行，卒，年六十二，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰貞，後更謚曰文。

translations.literal: Before departing he died, age sixty-two; posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Zhen — later changed to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office at sixty-two, was posthumously made Right Vice Director, first styled Zhen, later Wen.

sentences.zh: 貫之沈厚寡言，與人交，終歲無款曲，不為偽辭以悅人。

translations.literal: Guanzhi was deep and thick, few in words; with men in association — the whole year without intimate pleasantry — he did not make false words to please men.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and taciturn, he never flattered even in year-long acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 為右丞時，內僧造門曰：「君且相。」

translations.literal: When Right Vice Director, an inner monk came to the gate saying: "You will soon be chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Vice Director a monk told him he would soon be chancellor.

sentences.zh: 貫之命左右引出，曰：「此妄人也。」

translations.literal: Guanzhi ordered attendants to lead him out, saying: "This is a reckless man.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man thrown out as a fraud.

sentences.zh: 居輔相，嚴身律下，以正議裁物，室居無所改易。

translations.literal: Dwelling as assisting minister, he strictly disciplined himself and regulated subordinates, using upright discussion to judge things — the chamber dwelling had nothing changed.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he disciplined himself and judged by principle, changing nothing in his household.

sentences.zh: 裴均子持萬縑請撰先銘，答曰：「吾寧餓死，豈能為是哉！」

translations.literal: Pei Jun's son held ten thousand bolts of silk requesting composition of a forefather's inscription; he answered: "I would rather starve to death — how could I do this!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun's son offered ten thousand bolts for a funerary inscription. He replied, "I would rather starve.

sentences.zh: 生平未嘗通饋遺，故家無羨財。

translations.literal: In life he never once passed gifts — therefore the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He never accepted gifts and left no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 子澳，字子裴，第進士，復擢宏辭。

translations.literal: Son Ao, styled Zipi, passed jinshi, again was promoted hongci.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ao, courtesy name Zipi, passed the jinshi and hongci.

sentences.zh: 方靜寡欲，十年不肯調。

translations.literal: Square and quiet, few desires — ten years he would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Sedate and abstemious, he refused office for ten years.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞高元裕與其兄溫善，欲薦用之，諷澳謁己。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yuanyu was good with his elder brother Wen and wished to recommend and use him — hinted that Ao visit himself.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor Gao Yuanyu, friendly with his brother Wen, wanted to advance Ao and hinted he should call.

sentences.zh: 溫歸以告，澳不答。

translations.literal: Wen returned and told him; Ao did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wen told him; Ao did not reply.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「元裕端士，若輕之邪？」

translations.literal: Wen said: "Yuanyu is an upright gentleman — if you slight him?
translations.idiomatic: Wen said Yuanyu was upright and asked whether Ao slighted him.

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「然恐無呈身御史。」

translations.literal: Ao said: "Yet I fear there is no censor who presents his person."
translations.idiomatic: Ao said he feared there was no censor who curried favor by personal visits."

sentences.zh: 周墀節度鄭滑，表署幕府。

translations.literal: Zhou Chi was military commissioner of Zheng-Hua and memorialized him to the staff office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi of Zheng-Hua took him onto staff.

sentences.zh: 會墀入相，私謂曰：「何以教我？」

translations.literal: When Chi entered to be chancellor, he privately said: "By what will you teach me?
translations.idiomatic: When Chi became chancellor he asked privately what counsel Ao had.

sentences.zh: 澳曰：「願公無權。」

translations.literal: Ao said: "I wish that you, sir, have no power.
translations.idiomatic: Ao said, "Have no power.

sentences.zh: 墀愕眙，澳曰：「爵賞刑罰，人主之柄，公無以喜怒行之，俾庶官各舉其職，則公斂衽廟堂上，天下治矣。

translations.literal: Chi stared in shock; Ao said: "Rank, reward, punishment — the human lord's handle; you, sir, ought not use joy and anger to execute them; let the many offices each perform their duties — then you, sir, fold your robes in the temple hall and the realm is governed.
translations.idiomatic: Chi stared. Ao said rank, reward, and punishment belong to the throne; a minister should not wield them by mood, and if each officer did his duty the minister could govern folded in his robes.

sentences.zh: 烏用權？」

translations.literal: What use is power?
translations.idiomatic: What need of power?

sentences.zh: 墀嘆曰：「吾先居此，得無愧乎！」

translations.literal: Chi sighed: "I before dwelt here — can I be without shame!"
translations.idiomatic: Chi sighed that he had once held the same post without such wisdom."

sentences.zh: 擢考功員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Promoted Director of Evaluations, outer section, and History Office compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Evaluations and History Office compiler.

sentences.zh: 歲中知制誥，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Within the year he drafted edicts; summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he drafted edicts and entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎，進學士承旨。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted Vice Minister of War, advanced academician drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of War and chief Hanlin drafter.

sentences.zh: 與蕭寘皆為宣宗禮遇，每兩人直，必偕召問政得失。

translations.literal: With Xiao Zhen both received Xuanzong's courtesy; whenever the two were on duty, they were always summoned together to ask on government gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xiao Zhen were both favored; whenever on duty together Xuanzong questioned them on policy.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜被旨草詔書，事有不安者，即遷延須見帝，開陳可否，未嘗不順納。

translations.literal: He once at night received edict to draft a proclamation; when affairs had what was not secure, he then delayed and must see the emperor, opening and setting forth whether permitted — never not followed and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting at night, if a decree troubled him he delayed until he could advise the emperor, who always listened.

sentences.zh: 一日召入，屏左右問曰：「朕於敕使何如？」

translations.literal: One day summoned in, screened attendants and asked: "I toward edict envoys — how?
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor dismissed attendants and asked how he controlled edict commissioners.

sentences.zh: 澳陳帝威制前世無比。

translations.literal: Ao set forth that the emperor's authority surpassed past ages without compare.
translations.idiomatic: Ao said his authority surpassed all predecessors.

sentences.zh: 帝搖首曰：「未也。

translations.literal: The emperor shook his head: "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shook his head: "Not yet.

sentences.zh: 策安出？」

translations.literal: Where does the plan come out?
translations.idiomatic: What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 澳倉卒答曰：「若謀之外廷，則太和事可用追鑒，不若就擇可任者與計事。」

translations.literal: Ao in haste answered: "If plotting outside the outer court, then the Taihe affair can be used for retrospective warning — better to choose those who can be entrusted and plan affairs with them.
translations.idiomatic: Ao said quickly that the Taihe affair warned against outside plots, and trusted agents should be chosen instead.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕固行之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have solidly carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said he was already doing so.

sentences.zh: 自黃至綠，自綠至緋，猶可，衣紫即合為一矣。」

translations.literal: From yellow to green, from green to crimson — still possible; once clothed in purple they ought to be made one.
translations.idiomatic: From yellow to green to crimson was tolerable, but once in purple they should be treated as one body.

sentences.zh: 澳愧汗不能對，乃罷。

translations.literal: Ao sweated in shame and could not answer — then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ao sweated and could not answer, and the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹。

translations.literal: Changed to Jingzhao Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jingzhao governor.

sentences.zh: 帝舅鄭光主墅吏豪肆，積年不輸官賦，澳逮系之。

translations.literal: The emperor's uncle Zheng Guang's manor steward was domineering and extravagant, accumulating years not delivering official levies — Ao arrested and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's uncle Zheng Guang's steward bullied the district and withheld taxes for years until Ao arrested him.

sentences.zh: 它日延英，帝問其故。

translations.literal: Another day at Yanying, the emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying the emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 澳具道奸狀，且言必寘以法。

translations.literal: Ao fully set forth the wicked conduct, and said he must certainly place him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Ao detailed the crimes and insisted on legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可貸否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can he be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether mercy was possible.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「陛下自內署擢臣尹京邑，安可使畫一法獨行於貧下乎？」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Majesty from the inner office promoted me as governor of the capital district — how can I make uniform law run only on the poor below?
translations.idiomatic: He answered that law could not bend only for the powerful.

sentences.zh: 帝入白太后曰：「是不可犯。」

translations.literal: The emperor entered and told the Empress Dowager: "This one cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the empress dowager the case could not be violated.

sentences.zh: 後為輸租，乃免。

translations.literal: Afterward he delivered rent — then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Rent was paid and the man was released.

sentences.zh: 由是豪右斂跡。

translations.literal: From this the powerful and noble restrained their steps.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful then restrained themselves.

sentences.zh: 會戶部闕判使，帝以問澳，澳三不對。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue lacked a judging commissioner, the emperor with the question to Ao — Ao three times did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Revenue Ministry needed a supervising commissioner, the emperor asked Ao, who thrice kept silent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「任卿可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can I entrust you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether he could appoint him.

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣老矣，力疲氣耗，煩劇非所任者。」

translations.literal: He said: "I am old — strength weary, spirit spent — troublesome affairs are not what I can undertake.
translations.idiomatic: He said he was old and unfit for taxing work.

sentences.zh: 帝默不樂。

translations.literal: The emperor silently was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 出謂其甥柳玼曰：「吾本不為宰相知，上便委以使務，脫謂吾他岐而得，卒無以自白。
