translations.literal: Going out he told his nephew Liu Chi: "I originally was not known to the chancellor — the emperor then entrusted me with commission affairs; if released and said I obtained it by another branch, in the end there is no way to clear myself.
translations.idiomatic: He told his nephew Liu Chi that he had never sought finance office and feared being thought ambitious.

sentences.zh: 今時事浸惡，皆吾輩貪爵位致然。」

translations.literal: Now the time's affairs gradually worsen — all caused by us greedy for rank and position.
translations.idiomatic: He said the times worsened because officials clung to rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Before long, appointed Heyang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Heyang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝曰：「卿自便而遠我，非我去卿。」

translations.literal: Entering to take leave, the emperor said: "You yourself are convenient and distant from me — not that I remove you."
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave, the emperor said Ao chose distance, not dismissal."

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，徙平盧軍，入為吏部侍郎，復出為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: When Yizong was established, moved to Pinglu army; entered as Vice Minister of Personnel; again went out as Binning military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yizong he governed Pinglu, entered as Vice Minister of Personnel, and returned to Binning.

sentences.zh: 宰相杜審權素不悅澳，坐吏部時史盜簿書為奸，貶秘書監，分司東都。

translations.literal: Chancellor Du Shenquan from the beginning did not delight in Ao; because when in Personnel the clerks stole registry books to make wickedness, demoted Secretary Supervisor, stationed at eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Du Shenquan disliked him and, after registry theft in Personnel, demoted him to Secretary Supervisor at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 就遷河南尹，辭疾不拜，丐歸樊川。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Henan Governor; he declined illness and did not accept — begged return to Fanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon offered Henan governorship, he declined on illness and retired to Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以吏部侍郎召，不起。

translations.literal: Past a year, summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel — he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: A year later summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel, he refused.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈戶部尚書，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Vice Minister of Revenue, and styled Zhen.

sentences.zh: 澳在河陽累年，宣宗遣使至魏博，道出澳所，帝以簿紙手作詔賜澳曰：「密飭裝，秋當見卿。」

translations.literal: Ao at Heyang many years — Xuanzong sent envoy to Weibo, the route passing Ao's place; the emperor with paper in hand made an edict to bestow on Ao: "Secretly order your gear — in autumn I will see you.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang for years, Xuanzong sent an envoy to Weibo by way of Ao's post with a handwritten edict: "Prepare secretly — I will see you in autumn.

sentences.zh: 蓋將以為相也。

translations.literal: It covered intending to make him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was evidently to be made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 因問輔養術，澳具言金石非可禦，方士怪妄，宜斥遠之。

translations.literal: Because he asked on methods of nurturing, Ao fully said metals and stones cannot be used to ward off — alchemists' strange recklessness ought to be expelled and distanced.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about health, Ao said minerals and alchemists should be banished.

sentences.zh: 其八月，帝崩，不果相。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the emperor collapsed — it did not fruit as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor died, and the appointment never came.

sentences.zh: 為學士時，帝嘗曰：「朕每遣方鎮刺史，欲各悉州郡風俗者，卿為朕撰一書。」

translations.literal: When academician, the emperor once said: "I each time dispatch frontier prefects — I wish each to know thoroughly the prefectures' and districts' customs — you for me compose one book.
translations.idiomatic: As academician the emperor asked him to compile customs of every prefecture for frontier appointees.

sentences.zh: 澳乃取十道四方誌，手加紬次，題為《處分語》。

translations.literal: Ao then took the ten circuits' local gazetteers, by hand added collation, and titled it Instructions for Handling Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He collated the ten-circuit gazetteers by hand into Instructions for Handling Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後鄧州刺史薛弘宗中謝，帝敕戒州事，人人驚服。

translations.literal: Later Dengzhou Prefect Xue Hongzong attended thanksgiving; the emperor issued an edict admonition on prefectural affairs — every man was startled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong was dismissed, the emperor's admonition drawn from the book astonished every official.

sentences.zh: 綬，貫之兄。

translations.literal: Shou — Guanzhi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was Guanzhi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，又貢進士，禮部侍郎潘炎將以為舉首，綬以其友楊凝親老，故讓之，不對策輒去，凝遂及第。

translations.literal: He presented xiaolian, again presented jinshi; Vice Minister of Rites Pan Yan was about to make him first in the presentation — Shou because his friend Yang Ning's parents were old, therefore yielded to him, did not answer the policy questions and left — Ning then passed.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as xiaolian and jinshi, he was to head the list but yielded to Yang Ning, whose parents were aged, and left without answering the policy questions so Ning passed.

sentences.zh: 後擢明經，辟東都幕府。

translations.literal: Later promoted mingjing, recruited to eastern capital staff office.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed mingjing and joined the eastern capital staff.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，以左補闕為翰林學士，密政多所參逮。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time, with Left Remonstrator as Hanlin academician — secret government many times he participated in reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong he was left remonstrator and Hanlin academician, often privy to secret policy.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸其院，韋妃從，會綬方寢，學士鄭絪欲馳告之，帝不許，時大寒，以妃蜀𥜝袍覆而去，其待遇若此。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his courtyard; Consort Wei followed; it happened Shou was just sleeping — academician Zheng Yin wished to rush to inform him; the emperor did not permit; at the time great cold — with the consort's Shu brocade robe he covered and left — his treatment was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once visited while Shou slept; Zheng Yin would have waked him, but the emperor covered him with Consort Wei's robe in bitter cold and left quietly.

sentences.zh: 每入直，逾月不得休。

translations.literal: Each time entering duty, over a month he could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: On duty he sometimes went more than a month without rest.

sentences.zh: 以母老，屢丐解職，每請，帝輒不悅。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he repeatedly begged to resign office; each request the emperor then was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: His mother aged, he repeatedly sought release, each time displeasing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 出入八年，而性謹畏甚。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving eight years, yet his nature was very cautious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years in and out of court, yet he remained timid.

sentences.zh: 晚乃感心疾，罷還第，不極於用。

translations.literal: Late he then was moved by heart illness, dismissed to return to his residence — not fully used to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life heart trouble ended his service before his talent was fully used.

sentences.zh: 九月九日，帝為《黃菊歌》，顧左右曰：「安可不示韋綬！」

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the ninth month the emperor made the Song of Yellow Chrysanthemums, looked left and right and said: "How can we not show Wei Shou!
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth the emperor composed the Song of Yellow Chrysanthemums and said it must be shown to Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 即遣使持往，綬遽奉和，附使進。

translations.literal: He immediately sent envoy to carry it going; Shou hastily composed harmonizing verse, attached envoy and entered.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent; Shou hastily composed a reply and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為文不已，豈頤養邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Making literature without end — is this nourishing repose?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said endless writing was no way to rest.

sentences.zh: 敕自今勿復爾。

translations.literal: Edicted from now do not again do so.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to stop.

sentences.zh: 終左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He finally was Left Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Left Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 弟纁，有精識，為士林器許，兄弟皆名重當時。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xi had keen discernment, was by scholar-gentry vessels praised — the brothers all had heavy names in the time.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xi was esteemed for discernment; both brothers were famed.

sentences.zh: 綬子溫。

translations.literal: Shou's son Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's son was Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫，字弘育。

translations.literal: Wen, styled Hongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, courtesy name Hongyu.

sentences.zh: 方七歲，日誦書數千言。

translations.literal: At age seven, daily he recited books several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he recited thousands of characters daily.

sentences.zh: 十一，舉兩經及第，以拔萃高等補咸陽尉。

translations.literal: At eleven, presented both classics and passed; with exceptional grade from selection he was appointed Xianyang magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he passed both classics and with top selection grade became magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父愕然，疑假權謁進，召而試諸廷，文就無留意，喜曰：「兒無愧矣！」

translations.literal: His father was startled, suspected false authority and favor to advance; summoned and tested in the court — the writing was completed without lingering intent; he rejoiced and said: "The son is without shame!
translations.idiomatic: His father doubted favoritism, tested him at court, and rejoiced when he wrote effortlessly.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，以臺制苛嚴，不可以省養，不拜。

translations.literal: He entered as Investigating Censor; because the censorate's regulations were harsh and strict, he could not with reduced duties nurture parents — he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Made investigating censor, he declined because censorate rules forbade caring for parents.

sentences.zh: 換著作郎，既謝，輒解歸。

translations.literal: Exchanged to Composition Gentleman; having thanked, he immediately untied and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged for composition gentleman, thanked the court, and went home.

sentences.zh: 侍親疾，調適湯劑，彌二十年，衣不弛帶。

translations.literal: Attending parents' illness, adjusting decoctions — full twenty years, clothes never loosened belt.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed his parents twenty years without loosening his belt.

sentences.zh: 既居喪，毀瘠不支。

translations.literal: Once dwelling in mourning, he was emaciated and could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grew too thin to stand.

sentences.zh: 服除，李逢吉辟置宣武府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Li Fengji recruited and placed him in Xuanwu staff office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning Li Fengji took him onto the Xuanwu staff.

sentences.zh: 頻遷右補闕。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 宰相宋申錫被構，罪不測，溫倡曰：「丞相操履有初，不宜反，乃奸人陷之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Song Shenxi was framed — guilt uncertain — Wen initiated saying: "The chief minister's conduct from the beginning had constancy — it is not fitting to reverse; it is treacherous men who trapped him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Song Shenxi was framed, Wen declared the minister's conduct had been constant and traitors had trapped him.

sentences.zh: 吾等豈避雷霆，使上蒙霧咎邪！」

translations.literal: How can we avoid thunder and let the sovereign bear mist blame!
translations.idiomatic: How could they flee thunder and let the emperor bear blame!

sentences.zh: 率同舍伏閣切爭，由是益知名。

translations.literal: He led fellow lodge gentlemen to lie prostrate at the gate and argue urgently — from this he grew more known.
translations.idiomatic: He led colleagues to prostrate at the gate in protest and grew famous.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，太廟室漏罅，詔宗正、將作營治，不時畢，文宗怒，責卿李銳、監王堪，奪其稟，自敕中人葺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, the Ancestral Temple chambers leaked cracks; issued an edict the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Directorate of Public Works to repair — not finished in time; Wenzong was angry, blamed Director Li Rui and Supervisor Wang Kan, took away their salaries — himself issued an edict inner attendants to repair.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 the ancestral temple leaked; Wenzong, angry at delay, stripped officials and ordered eunuchs to repair.

sentences.zh: 溫諫：「吏舉其職，國以治；

translations.literal: Wen remonstrated: "Officials perform their duties — the state thereby is governed;
translations.idiomatic: Wen remonstrated that officials must do their duties for the state to be governed;

sentences.zh: 事歸於正，法以修。

translations.literal: affairs return to correctness — law thereby is repaired.
translations.idiomatic: and affairs return to law when duties are clear.

sentences.zh: 夫設制度，立官司，度經費，則宗廟最重也。

translations.literal: Setting institutions, establishing offices, measuring expenses — then the ancestral temple is most heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions, offices, and budgets make the ancestral temple the weightiest charge.

sentences.zh: 比詔下閱月，有司弛墯不力，正可黜慢官，懲不恪，擇可任者繕完之，則吏舉職，事歸正矣。

translations.literal: Compared with the edict issued a month — the responsible offices were slack and did not exert force; properly one could dismiss negligent officials, punish the not reverent, choose those who can be entrusted to complete repair — then officials perform duty, affairs return to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: A month after the edict the offices had slackened; negligent officials should be punished and able men chosen to finish repairs.

sentences.zh: 今慢吏奪稟，而易以中人，是許百司公廢職，以宗廟之重，為陛下所私，臣竊惜之。

translations.literal: Now negligent officials' salaries are taken and easily exchanged for inner men — this is permitting the hundred offices publicly to abandon duty; with the ancestral temple's heaviness made the emperor's private matter — I privately regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing them with eunuchs let every office abandon duty and made the temple the emperor's private affair, which he regretted.

sentences.zh: 請還將作，則官修業矣。」

translations.literal: Please return to the Directorate of Public Works — then offices repair their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Directorate of Public Works be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝乃罷宦人。

translations.literal: The emperor then dismissed the eunuch men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dismissed the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 會群臣請上尊號，溫固諫：「今河南水，江淮旱歉，京師雪積五尺，老稚凍仆，此非崇飾虛名時。」

translations.literal: When the ministers together requested superior title for the emperor, Wen firmly remonstrated: "Now Henan has flood water, Huai and Yangtze drought and poor harvest, the capital snow piled five feet — old and young freeze and fall — this is not the time to exalt and adorn empty names.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers sought a honorific title, Wen objected that floods, drought, and snow made it no time for empty honors.

sentences.zh: 帝順納，乃謝群臣。

translations.literal: The emperor followed and accepted; then apologized to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted and apologized to the court.

sentences.zh: 改侍御史。

translations.literal: Changed to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 李德裕入輔，擢禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu entered to assist, he promoted Vice Director of Rites, outer section.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu became chancellor he promoted Wen to outer Vice Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 或言雅為牛僧孺厚，德裕曰：「是子堅正，可以私廢乎？」

translations.literal: Some said he was from old thick with Niu Sengru; Deyu said: "This son is firm and upright — can he be abandoned for private reason?
translations.idiomatic: Some said Wen favored Niu Sengru; Deyu replied that uprightness should not be sacrificed to faction.

sentences.zh: 鄭註節度鳳翔，表為副，溫曰：「拒則遠黜，從之禍不測，吾焉能為註起邪？」

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu was military commissioner of Fengxiang; memorialized him as deputy; Wen said: "If refused then distant demotion; if followed then disaster cannot be measured — how can I act for Zhu and rise?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu of Fengxiang wanted him as deputy; Wen said refusal meant exile and acceptance meant ruin, and he would not rise through Zhu.

sentences.zh: 註誅，由考功員外郎拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhu was executed, from Director of Evaluations, outer section, he was appointed Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu's execution he was made Remonstrance Grandee from Director of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Before long, Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 先是，綬在禁廷，積憂畏病廢，故誡溫不得任近職，至是固辭。

translations.literal: Before this, Shou in the forbidden court accumulated worry and fear, illness dismissed — therefore admonished Wen not to accept near office; to this he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, worn by fear in the palace, had warned Wen against near office, and Wen firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「寧綬治命邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Would you treat Shou's dying command?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily asked whether he obeyed a deathbed command.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎崔蠡曰：「溫用亂命，益所以為孝。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Cui Li said: "Wen using disorderly command — all the more therefore is filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Cui Li said disobeying a confused command was filial.

sentences.zh: 帝意釋，換知制誥。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent released; exchanged to drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and made him a drafter.

sentences.zh: 引疾徙太常少卿。

translations.literal: Citing illness moved to Vice Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He cited illness and became Vice Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 宰相李固言薦溫給事中，帝曰：「溫素避事，肯為我論駁乎？

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Guyan recommended Wen as Supervising Censor; the emperor said: "Wen from old avoids affairs — willing to debate and refute for me?
translations.idiomatic: Li Guyan recommended him as supervising censor; the emperor doubted whether the retiring Wen would debate.

sentences.zh: 須太子長，以為賓客。」

translations.literal: Must wait until the Crown Prince is long — make him guest.
translations.idiomatic: He said to wait until the heir grew and make Wen his tutor.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒為給事中。

translations.literal: After a long time, he finally became Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he became supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 初，兼莊恪太子侍讀，晨詣宮，日中見太子，諫曰：「殿下盛年，宜雞鳴蚤作，問安天子，如文王故事。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, concurrently Zhuangyi Crown Prince lecturing reader; morning he went to the palace, midday he saw the Crown Prince; he remonstrated: "Your Highness in flourishing years — ought at cockcrow early to rise, inquire after the Son of Heaven's peace — like King Wen's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: As tutor to the heir he urged the young prince to rise at dawn and inquire after the emperor as King Wen had.

sentences.zh: 太子不悅。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was displeased.

sentences.zh: 辭侍讀，見聽。

translations.literal: He resigned lecturing reader; the request was heard.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 王晏平罷靈武節度使，以馬及鎧仗自隨，貶康州司戶參軍，厚賂貴近，浹日，改撫州司馬，樂工尉遲璋授光州長史，溫悉封上詔書。

translations.literal: Wang Yanping dismissed from Lingwu military commission — with horses and armor and weapons following himself — demoted to Kangzhou army registrar; thick bribes to the noble and near — in a few days changed to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang granted Guangzhou chief administrator — Wen all sealed and submitted the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanping left Lingwu with horses and armor, bribed his way from Kangzhou registrar to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang was made Guangzhou chief administrator — Wen sealed and returned all such edicts.

sentences.zh: 太子得罪，詔諭群臣，溫曰：「陛下訓之不早，非獨太子罪。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince offended; edict instructed the ministers; Wen said: "Your Majesty trained him not early — not alone the Crown Prince's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir fell, Wen told the court the emperor had trained him too late, not the heir alone.

sentences.zh: 時頗直其言。

translations.literal: At the time many straightened his words.
translations.idiomatic: Many then praised his frankness.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Promoted Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵推官姚勖按大獄，帝以為能，擢職方員外郎，將趨省，溫使戶止，即上言：「郎官清選，不可賞能吏。」

translations.literal: Salt and Iron investigating official Yao Xu according to great cases — the emperor considered him able, promoted Director of the Bureau of Appointments, outer section; about to hurry to the ministry, Wen sent household to stop — immediately above spoke: "Gentleman-officer clear selection — cannot reward able clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xu, praised for prosecutions, was to enter the Bureau of Appointments; Wen blocked him, saying clear offices must not reward mere clerical skill.

sentences.zh: 帝命中人諭送，溫執議不移，詔改勖檢校禮部郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a eunuch to instruct and send — Wen held discussion without moving; issued an edict to change Xu to honorary Ritual Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch to insist; Wen held firm until Xu was made honorary ritual director.

sentences.zh: 帝問故於楊嗣復，對曰：「勖，名臣後，治行無疵。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason of Yang Sifu; he answered: "Xu is a famous minister's descendant — governing conduct without blemish.
translations.idiomatic: Asked by Yang Sifu, he said Xu was a famous minister's heir without fault.

sentences.zh: 若吏材幹而不入清選，佗日孰肯當劇事者？

translations.literal: If clerkly talent and capability yet not entering clear selection — in another day who will be willing to undertake arduous affairs?
translations.idiomatic: If clerical talent bypassed clear selection, who would later take hard posts?

sentences.zh: 此衰晉風，不可以法。」

translations.literal: This is declining Jin wind — it cannot be law.
translations.idiomatic: That was the decay of Jin and must not become law.

sentences.zh: 帝素重溫，出為陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: The emperor from old valued Wen; sent out as Shan-Guo observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor valued him, Wen was sent to Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 民當輸租而麥未熟，吏白督之，溫曰：「使民貨田中穗以供賦，可乎？」

translations.literal: The people ought to deliver rent while wheat was not yet ripe; clerks reported to press them; Wen said: "Make the people carry grain spikes in the fields to supply levies — can it be?
translations.idiomatic: When wheat was unripe clerks pressed rent; Wen asked whether spikes in the field should pay tax.

sentences.zh: 為緩期而賦辦。

translations.literal: He for them extended the period and the levy was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He granted delay and the levy was still met.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was established, he was promoted Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong he became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 李德裕欲引同輔政，溫苦言李漢可釋，德裕悵然，出宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Li Deyu wished to draw him in to assist in government; Wen bitterly said Li Han could be released — Deyu regretfully, sent out as Xuan-She observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu wanted him as chancellor; Wen urged releasing Li Han instead, and Deyu sent him to Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 池民訟刺史，劾無狀，榜殺之，威行部中。

translations.literal: Chizhou people sued the prefect — impeachment without substance — he posted and killed him; authority ran through the department.
translations.idiomatic: At Chizhou he posted and killed a prefect falsely accused by the people, and his authority ran the circuit.

sentences.zh: 既疾，召親屬，賦綬詩「在室愧屋漏」，因泣下曰：「今知沒身不負斯誡矣！」

translations.literal: Once ill, he summoned kin; composed Shou's poem "In the chamber ashamed before roof leak," and weeping said: "Now I know dying body does not betray this admonition!
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he summoned kin, quoted Shou's verse on shame before a leaking roof, and wept that he had kept the teaching.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，贈工部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: He died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight, was posthumously Minister of Works, and styled Xiao.

sentences.zh: 溫性剛峻，人望見無敢戲慢者。

translations.literal: Wen's nature was firm and steep — men seeing him did not dare jest or slight.
translations.idiomatic: Firm and stern, none dared jest before him.

sentences.zh: 與楊嗣復、李玨善，嘗勸與李德裕平故憾，二人不從，及皆謫，溫嘆曰：「用吾言，孰至是邪！」

translations.literal: With Yang Sifu and Li Jue good — he once urged reconciling with Li Deyu old resentments — the two did not follow; when all were demoted, Wen sighed: "If my words had been used — who would arrive at this!
translations.idiomatic: Friendly with Yang Sifu and Li Jue, he urged reconciliation with Li Deyu; when all were exiled he sighed that his counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 一女，歸薛蒙。

translations.literal: One daughter — married to Xue Meng.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter married Xue Meng.

sentences.zh: 女工屬文，續曹大家《女訓》，行於世。

translations.literal: Female craft adept at literature — continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women — circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in letters, she continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women.

sentences.zh: 溫少合，所善惟蕭祐。

translations.literal: Wen in youth harmonized — those he favored were only Xiao You.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his only close friend was Xiao You.

sentences.zh: 祐者，字祐之，夷淡君子也。

translations.literal: You — styled Youzhi — a mild and detached gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: You, courtesy name Youzhi, was a mild recluse.

sentences.zh: 少貧窶，隱居，以孝養聞。

translations.literal: In youth poor and cramped, he hid and dwelt — with filial nurturing was heard.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he lived in seclusion famed for filial care.

sentences.zh: 司農卿李實督官租，祐居喪，未及輸，召至，將責之。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Li Shi supervised official rent; You dwelt in mourning, not yet having delivered — summoned to arrive, about to blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Shi, collecting rent, summoned You in mourning before payment.

sentences.zh: 會有賜與，倩祐為奏，實稱善，即薦於朝。

translations.literal: It happened there was imperial bestowal — he borrowed You to compose memorial — Shi praised it well, immediately recommended to court.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial gift required a memorial; You drafted it, Li Shi praised it, and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 終制，以處士拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, with reclusive scholar status appointed Left Collector.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made Left Collector as a recluse scholar.

sentences.zh: 累遷諫議大夫，終桂州觀察使，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted Remonstrance Grandee — finally Guilin observation commissioner; posthumously made Right Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Remonstrance Grandee and ended as Guilin commissioner, posthumously Right Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 精畫及書，自鐘、王、蕭、張以來，皆能識其真。

translations.literal: Keen in painting and calligraphy — from Zhong, Wang, Xiao, Zhang onward, all could distinguish the true.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in painting and calligraphy, he could authenticate works from Zhong You to Zhang Xu.

sentences.zh: 謷然不以塵事自蒙，故溫號「山林友」云。

translations.literal: Lofty and not with worldly affairs to veil himself — therefore Wen called him "mountain-forest friend.
translations.idiomatic: Above worldly vanity, Wen called him a mountain-and-forest friend.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：杜黃裳善謀，裴垍能持法，李藩鯁挺，韋貫之忠實，皆足穆天縡，經國體，撥衰奮王，菑攘四方。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Du Huangshang was good at planning, Pei Ji could hold law, Li Fan was upright and stiff, Wei Guanzhi was loyal and solid — all sufficient to harmonize heaven's weave, regulate the state's body, stir the declining and rouse the king, clear away calamities on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says Du Huangshang planned well, Pei Ji upheld law, Li Fan was blunt, Wei Guanzhi was loyal — all fit to harmonize heaven's pattern, restore the state, rouse a failing throne, and clear troubles on every side.

sentences.zh: 憲宗中興，寧不謂得人而致然邪？

translations.literal: Xianzong's restoration — would one not say it was obtaining men and thereby achieving it?
translations.idiomatic: Was Xianzong's restoration not the fruit of finding such men?

sentences.zh: 昔子貢孔堂高第而貨殖，韓安國漢名宰而資貪，黃裳亦以受餉見疵，至於忠烈峣然，則不可掩已。

translations.literal: Formerly Zigong was Confucius' hall high graduate yet did commerce; Han Anguo was Han's famed chancellor yet was greedy in goods — Huangshang also because of receiving gifts was seen blemished; as to loyal martyrdom towering — that cannot be covered.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong was Confucius' foremost disciple yet traded; Han Anguo was a famed Han minister yet greedy; Huangshang too was blemished by gifts — yet loyal heroism cannot be hidden.
